title: A form marks commitment level rather than procedure content
summary: A semantic operator distinguishes an asserted procedure from a conditional or hypothetical procedure, while leaving the procedure’s lexical content unresolved.

design.mechanism: asserted/conditional commitment versus ordinary procedure marker
design.unit: held complete constructions or paired reading contexts
design.contrast: Matched records with the same operation frame should differ in an independently observable commitment cue; an ordinary procedure marker predicts identical commitment status.
design.prediction: IDEA000070 is a nearby raw hypothesis, but this design requires a held same-procedure contrast and explicitly tests commitment scope rather than an evidential word gloss.
design.countermodel: A surface-copying, renderer, or context-conditioned convention can mimic training observations without the proposed semantic mechanism.
design.falsifier: The candidate varies with operation content while commitment cues stay fixed, or no same-frame contrast exists.
design.principal_risk: No independent authorial commitment annotation exists; source punctuation/layout cannot be assumed to be semantic.
design.smallest_test: Freeze two same-frame records and one contrastive record, define commitment cues before inspection, and test whether the candidate form tracks only commitment.
design.prior_duplicate_pointers: Related to IDEA000070; retain as distinct only if a same-frame held contrast is obtainable.
design.selection_status: raw unreviewed; no readiness or novelty claim
